details: CONFIRMED by reading: before 07d54ab9 every group ran with timeout=_left() of CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT, so the message's number was
the budget used. 07d54ab9 gives the registry group float(STEP_TIMEOUT) but leaves the shared message, which still prints
CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT. Reachable on the loaded machine the commit was written for. The break also skips the changed tests, as
evidence: lib/relay_precheck.py:171  limit = float(STEP_TIMEOUT) if group == [RULES_REGISTRY_TEST] else _left()
lib/relay_precheck.py:176  failed.append("FAIL changed tests took longer than %d s" % CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT)
failing_case: Machine loaded so tests.test_rules_gate.RuleTestsComplete takes over 60 s (the brief's own case: python took over a minute to
start at load 50). check_changed_tests now runs it with timeout=STEP_TIMEOUT (60), it times out, and the except branch appends
"FAIL changed tests took longer than 230 s" (CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT) and breaks, so the changed tests never run.
Now: the line names 230 s although the cut came at 60 s, and the person looks for a slow changed test that does not exist.
Should: the line names the registry test and the 60 s it was given (or the budget actually used), e.g.
"FAIL rules registry test took longer than 60 s".
fix_hint: In the except branch, print the limit actually used and which group: "FAIL %s took longer than %d s" % ("rules registry test"
if group == [RULES_REGISTRY_TEST] else "changed tests", limit-or-budget); add pass case 1 as a test.
pass_cases: 1. STEP_TIMEOUT=1, CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT=230, a registry stand-in that sleeps 3 s: the output holds a line naming the registry
test and "1 s", and no "took longer than 230 s".
2. CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT=2, a changed test sleeping 60 s, healthy registry: "  FAIL changed tests took longer than 2 s"
3. A red registry stand-in and a 60 s changed test with CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT=1: both "RuleTestsComplete" and
"took longer than 1 s" appear (test_a_slow_changed_test_does_not_hide_the_registry_message keeps passing).
findings.summary: a registry test cut off at its new 60 s allowance is reported as 'changed tests took longer than 230 s'

details: First half CONFIRMED (reproduced: head test on master's precheck, OK x3). Second half PLAUSIBLE: needs a run under load; the
reasoning is that _git uses timeout=_left() of the same 1 s deadline set in run() before check_changed_tests starts.
Rated MEDIUM because it is the quality-gate rule (flaky proven by 20 clean runs) and the user rule "for a regression test,
check that it fails with the fix disabled"; the brief also says each new test is shown to fail without the fix.
Size: 20 agent minutes (one test with a slow registry stand-in, then a 20-run loop).
evidence: cp head tests/test_precheck.py into a master worktree; python3 tests/run_unittest.py
gate 407c9068: AssertionError 'RuleTestsComplete' not found ... FAIL changed tests took longer than 3 s
failing_case: Disable the fix (master's lib/relay_precheck.py, registry run with timeout=_left()) and run head's
test_a_slow_changed_test_does_not_hide_the_registry_message: it passes (3 of 3 runs OK at load 11). So nothing pins the new
behaviour "the registry test keeps its own allowance". And the test now sets CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT=1 (was 3): the git calls in
changed_test_modules (merge-base, diff, ls-files) share that 1 s deadline; at load 50 a git call over 1 s raises TimeoutExpired
in run(), giving "FAIL changed tests took longer than 1 s" without "RuleTestsComplete", the same red the commit set out to fix.
Should: a test that fails when the registry group gets _left() instead of its own allowance, and the flaky test shown clean over
max(20, ceil(3/p)) runs (rule: Quality gate, "a flaky test is a bug, proven fixed with max(20, ceil(3/p)) clean runs").
fix_hint: Make the registry stand-in in the test sleep longer than CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT (e.g. 2 s with budget 1 s) so only the own
allowance lets its verdict show; keep the budget for the git calls separate or raise the test's budget so git is not cut off;
run the test 20 times and record it.
pass_cases: 1. Registry stand-in that sleeps 2 s and is red, CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT=1, STEP_TIMEOUT left at 60, a 60 s changed test: output
holds "RuleTestsComplete" and "took longer than 1 s"; with the registry run on _left() the same test fails.
2. test_a_slow_changed_test_does_not_hide_the_registry_message: 20 consecutive clean runs, recorded with the load average.
reason: tests/test_precheck.py test_a_slow_changed_test_does_not_hide_the_registry_message (line 294): registry stand-in sleeps 5 s above the 3 s budget; passes on head, fails with the registry on the remaining budget (07d54ab9^). 20-run claim is the fixer's, not repeated.
findings.summary: the precheck fix has no test that fails without it, and the flaky test may stay flaky with a 1 s budget (quality gate)
